I smoked a pack a day for almost a decade, with intermittent attempts to stop. I read the book The Easy Way to Stop Smoking by Alan Carr, and it worked for me. The premise is that you smoke freely while you read the book, and by the end of it you're ready to walk away from cigarettes for good. It deprograms the psychology we use around smoking to help make it easy to leave it behind. Things like, every time you have a cigarette you reset the clock til the next one, and how can something be both relaxing (the end of day cigarette) and energizing (the first cigarette of the day.) I'm not impressionable with mumbo jumbo, and read it VERY critically. It's repetitive on certain points, but hammers them home.
Zyban + Patches. Worked like a charm. Zero cravings plus bonus mood elevation.

In my experience I've done best when I take it one day at a time rather than "after x date, no more cigs". Just wake up one morning and tell yourself "I'm not going to smoke today" and so on. That helped me get past the anxiety of the looming quitting date. Oh, and failure is all part of the process. I've quit about six times or so but every time I do I make it a little longer. Just like with most things there is no "one weird trick to success" its all about persistence, odds are you will fail so dust yourself off and just keep trying.
Remind yourself that you are stronger than the drug. Keep digging deeper and deeper. You have it in you. Source - me, addictive personality, cigarette free for 14 years, cold turkey.
